verdict.rationale: Fivetran's docs say its connectors sync to 'your data warehouse or data lake', including data lakes in open table formats, and it has a supported-destinations page. Its MCP tooling can copy existing connections to a new destination with configs and schemas intact, which supports portability without rebuilding pipelines. However, only Snowflake and BigQuery are confirmed as destinations, and only by community posts; the destinations page is just a title. Missing for 10: first-party documentation naming Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Postgres and object storage as supported destinations; evidence that destination switching works without pipeline changes outside the MCP copy tool; independent corroboration for Databricks, Postgres and object-storage loading.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I load to the major warehouses and lakes — Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Postgres, object storage — without changing pipelines

citations.quote: Fivetran provides pre-built data connectors that automatically sync data from your applications, databases, event streams, and files to your data warehouse or data lake.
Automatically sync query‑ready, fully‑managed data to your data lake in open table formats.
Copy existing Fivetran connections to a new destination. Keep their configs and schemas intact or modify them as you like.
Ingest with Fivetran, transform with DBT and store in Snowflake.
Fivetran's free plan has met my needs to sync data from different ad platforms to BigQuery pretty well
